'''William Julius Green''' (born July 28, 1981) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who currently is an assistant coach for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played professionally in the NBA with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[New Orleans Hornets]], [[Atlanta Hawks]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], and [[Orlando Magic]]. He was selected in the second round (41st pick overall) of the [[2003 NBA draft]] by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] and later acquired by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] from Seattle in a draft-night trade for the draft rights to [[Paccelis Morlende]] (50th pick overall) and cash considerations.

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia 76ers (2003–2010)===
Green was a 1999 graduate of [[Cooley High School]]; after a college career at the [[University of Detroit Mercy]], he was selected by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in the second round (41st overall) of the [[2003 NBA draft]]. He was traded the same day to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]<ref name=re-signs>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2381184 Green returns to Sixers after aborted summer deal - NBA - ESPN]</ref> for the draft rights to [[Paccelis Morlende]] and cash considerations.

Green was due to re-sign with the Sixers during the 2005 offseason, but suffered an injury the day of the contract signing, which put the contract in a state of limbo. On March 23, 2006, he officially re-signed with the Sixers,<ref name=re-signs/> and on April 4, 2006, he was activated and played 11 minutes, scoring 9 points on 4-for-6 shooting in a loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2004/year/2006/willie-green Willie Green Game By Game Stats and Performance - Atlanta Hawks - ESPN]</ref>

Green, in the final Sixers game of the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], had a career-high 37 points against the [[Toronto Raptors]] on April 4, 2007.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20200920121059/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270418028 Philadelphia 76ers vs. Toronto Raptors - Recap - April 18, 2007 - ESPN]</ref>

Green beat out [[Rodney Carney]] for the Sixers starting [[shooting guard]] position. During the [[2007–08 NBA season]], Green had career highs in games played (74, all of them as a starter), minutes played (26.6), field goal percentage (.436), rebounds (2.5), assists (2.0), and points (12.4).

===New Orleans Hornets (2010–2011)===
Green was traded to New Orleans with forward [[Jason Smith (American basketball)|Jason Smith]] in exchange for forward [[Darius Songaila]] and rookie forward [[Craig Brackins]] on September 23, 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5607517|title=Rookie Craig Brackins traded to 76ers|date=September 23, 2010}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2011–2012)===
On December 22, 2011, Green signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8907 Atlanta Hawks sign guard Willie Green]</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2012–2014)===
On July 30, 2012, Green was signed-and-traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the rights to [[Sofoklis Schortsanitis]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-acquire-guard-willie-green-atlanta CLIPPERS ACQUIRE GUARD WILLIE GREEN FROM ATLANTA]</ref><ref>[https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-send-willie-green-clippers-sign-and-trade-deal ATLANTA HAWKS SEND WILLIE GREEN TO CLIPPERS IN SIGN-AND-TRADE DEAL]</ref>

On June 29, 2014, he was waived by the Clippers.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-waive-willie-green CLIPPERS WAIVE WILLIE GREEN]</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2014–2015)===
On June 30, 2014, Green was claimed off waivers by the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-claim-willie-green-waivers Magic Claim Willie Green Off Waivers]</ref>

==Coaching career==
=== Assistant coach (2016–2021) ===
On August 9, 2016, Green was hired by the [[Golden State Warriors]] coaching staff as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-hire-willie-green-assistant-coach/player-development|title=Warriors Hire Willie Green as Assistant Coach/Player Development|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=August 9, 2016|access-date=August 9, 2016}}</ref> He won his first championship when the Warriors defeated the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in five games of the [[2017 NBA Finals]]. Green won his second straight championship when the Warriors defeated the Cavaliers in four games of the [[2018 NBA Finals]].

On June 26, 2019, he was hired as an assistant coach for the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/06/26/suns-complete-coaching-staff-official-release/|title=Phoenix Suns announce complete coaching staff|website=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref>

=== New Orleans Pelicans (2021–2025)===
On July 22, 2021, Green was named head coach of the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Willie Green named New Orleans Pelicans head coach|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/willie-green-named-new-head-coach-new-orleans-pelicans|website=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2021|accessdate=July 22, 2021}}</ref> After starting the season 1–12, Green led the Pelicans to a 36–46 record, finishing ninth in the Western Conference and securing a spot in the [[NBA play-in tournament]]. The Pelicans would go on to beat the [[San Antonio Spurs]] and the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] en route to their first playoff berth since the [[2017–18 New Orleans Pelicans season|2017–18 season]]. Green and the Pelicans would ultimately fall to the [[Phoenix Suns]], Green's former team, in six games in the First Round.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Guillory |first1=William |title=Pelicans, who kept believing after a 1–12 start, clinch a Play-In Tournament spot |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3233276/2022/04/06/pelicans-who-kept-believing-after-a-1-12-start-clinch-a-play-in-tournament-spot/ |work=The Athletic}}</ref>

Green and the Pelicans started the [[2022–23 New Orleans Pelicans season|2022–23 season]] off strong, tied with the [[Denver Nuggets]] for first place in the Western Conference at the start of 2023 with a 23–12 record.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kimble |first1=Tracy |title=Pelicans Win Duel With Suns, Remain Best in the West |url=https://www.si.com/nba/pelicans/nba/pelicans-win-duel-with-suns-1st-place-in-west |website=SI|date=December 10, 2022 }}</ref> However, injuries to multiple players, including [[Zion Williamson]] and [[Brandon Ingram]], saw the team regress significantly during the second half of the season. The Pelicans finished ninth in the Western Conference, qualifying for the play-in tournament for the second consecutive season. Their season ended with a 123–118 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on April 12, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last1=AP |title=Gilgeous-Alexander leads Thunder past Pelicans in play-in |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401539674 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Despite their struggles, Green and the Pelicans finished the regular season with a 42–40 record, marking Green's first winning season as a head coach. 

After a 2–10 start to the [[2025–26 New Orleans Pelicans season|2025–26 season]], placing New Orleans at the bottom of the Western Conference, Green was fired on November 15, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans relieve Willie Green of head coaching duties|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/willie-green-relieved-head-coaching-duties-new-orleans-pelicans-head-coach-james-borrego|website=NBA.com|date=November 15, 2025|access-date=November 15, 2025}}</ref>

=== Dallas Mavericks (2026–present) ===
On July 2, 2026, Green was hired by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] as the lead assistant coach under head coach [[Dusty May]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Former Pelicans Head Coach Willie Green Lands New NBA Job|url=https://www.si.com/nba/pelicans/onsi/former-pelicans-head-coach-willie-green-lands-new-nba-job-01kwhv6by9n1|website=si.com|date=July 2, 2026 |access-date=July 13, 2026}}</ref>
